title: DeepSeek API Pricing 2026: Cost per 1M Tokens
summary: DeepSeek API pricing charges separate rates for cache-hit input, cache-miss input, and output tokens. Categorize your usage to determine actual costs.
body_markdown:
## What 1,000 automation runs cost per model


Once you have your own usage figures, the arithmetic is short. 1,000 runs of a two-step flow cost about $0.43 on DeepSeek V4.1-Flash and about $0.09 on Qwen 3.7 Flash, so the cheaper model is **roughly five times less** .


### Token assumptions for each step


I assume a summarised email is 1,500 tokens in and 200 out, and a classified ticket is 500 in and 20 out. Swap in your own averages, because long email threads will move the input side far more than the output side.


Quoted as input–output dollars per million tokens, the rates come from[GetAPIPulse](https://www.getapipulse.com/top-10-cheapest-llm-apis.html) . DeepSeek V4.1-Flash is $0.15–$0.60, the highest in this budget group. Qwen 3.7 Flash is $0.03–$0.13, the lowest, so it's the comparison here.


In that listing, the next cheapest was GPT-5 nano at $0.05–$0.40, an older model; OpenAI's current efficient option is GPT-6 Luna, which that listing did not price.[Gemini](https://gemini.google/subscriptions) Flash-Lite at $0.10–$0.40 and[Claude](https://claude.com/pricing) Haiku 5.5 at $0.10–$0.50 both sit between the two extremes, so any of them undercuts DeepSeek on list price.


### Cost per 1,000 runs, side by side


Look at the table and the gap is proportional, not dramatic: the cheaper model costs about a fifth at every volume, so the saving only matters once volume grows.


Step Tokens in / out DeepSeek, 1,000 runs Qwen 3.7 Flash, 1,000 runs 10k runs a month (DeepSeek / Qwen) 100k runs a month (DeepSeek / Qwen)


Summarise email 1,500 / 200 $0.345 $0.071 $3.45 / $0.71 $34.50 / $7.10


Classify ticket 500 / 20 $0.087 $0.018 $0.87 / $0.18 $8.70 / $1.76


Total 2,000 / 220 $0.432 $0.089 $4.32 / $0.89 $43.20 / $8.86


At 10,000 runs a month the difference is about $3.40, which isn't worth an engineering afternoon. At 100,000 runs it is about $34 a month, still small, so quality should decide the choice before price does.


This is list-price arithmetic. Cache hits would lower DeepSeek's input cost, and reasoning tokens would raise its output cost, which is why your own measured usage should replace my assumptions.


Of the two, classification is the safest step to move to the cheaper model. It produces 20 output tokens and has a checkable answer, so you can compare its labels against DeepSeek's on a sample before switching.


Routing each step to its own model lets you keep DeepSeek only where the summaries need it, and that only pays if splitting the flow is free.


In Activepieces it is: each step can call its own model through the DeepSeek integration, and the flow is metered at 1 credit per run, so the ten-step version costs what the two-step workaround did.


Zapier bills per task and Make per module, so on those a finer split raises the automation bill and charges the builder for the step-by-step design that makes the routing worthwhile.
